## 固定收益市場主線

油價反彈，加上聯準會官員再度呼籲收緊政策，壓過Nvidia領導層危機引發的早盤避險買盤，美國公債轉為下跌。2年期殖利率上升14.37個基點至4.8814%，10年期上升13.75個基點至5.1271%。退伍軍人節休市後恢復交易，通膨與預期升息步調對債市的影響，大於科技股下跌。

美國總統川普表示，美國可以不與伊朗達成協議，令外交進展帶來的樂觀情緒部分逆轉。即使美國原油與成品油庫存大增，布蘭特原油期貨仍上漲3.24%至每桶$95.77。克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack主張更頻繁、小幅度升息；舊金山聯準銀行總裁Mary Daly則表示，企業正考慮轉嫁成本，可能仍須進一步緊縮。兩人的談話鞏固政策收緊方向，但12月升息幅度仍有分歧。

信用市場對股市震盪與借款人融資前景作出不同評價。Nvidia撤換黃仁勳，由財務長Colette Kress暫代執行長，但其信用違約保護成本先升後降。Alphabet完成近$40億等值的亞洲本幣借款；CoreWeave更具體的擔保融資計畫也帶動債券走強。與此同時，市場再度出現警訊，質疑債券投資人能否持續承接AI產業龐大的資金需求。

## 油價與升息主張扭轉美債早盤漲勢

Nvidia前景的不確定性，最初支撐長天期美國公債。恢復交易的早盤，30年期殖利率一度下降3個基點至5.32%，10年期則在4.99%左右持穩。澳洲聯邦銀行的Carol Kong認為，這股溫和避險需求，來自市場對這家AI投資熱潮核心企業的疑慮。短端當時已受到通膨與聯準會進一步升息預期壓抑。

隨著能源價格上漲、決策官員強化緊縮理由，早盤支撐消退。收盤時，5年期殖利率上升15.11個基點至4.9704%，為主要付息年期中升幅最大者；30年期上升9.97個基點至5.4521%。2年與10年期利差收窄0.62個基點至24.57個基點，2年與30年期利差縮小4.4個基點至57.07個基點。投資人持有比政策敏感年期更長的公債，所能取得的額外殖利率持續受到壓縮。

這波調整集中在短端，從一週變化尤其明顯：2年期殖利率上升41.91個基點，10年與30年期分別上升29.24與19.82個基點。若與一個月前相比，2年期上升9.45個基點，10年與30年期仍分別低11.07與14.35個基點。近期政策路徑雖急遽重估，較長期間累積的長天期公債漲幅仍保留一部分。

週四10年期殖利率升幅主要來自實質借款成本提高，通膨補償也同步上升。10年期抗通膨公債實質殖利率上升9.59個基點至2.8662%，損益兩平通膨率上升4.16個基點至2.2609%。過去一週，實質殖利率上升26.85個基點，損益兩平通膨率則上升2.39個基點。油價回升增添通膨因素，但這波美債賣壓仍以實質殖利率上升為主。

川普稱華府不需要伊朗協議，並指示副總統范斯將重心轉向國內事務。此前，中東供應恢復跡象與外交解決的希望曾壓低油價；他的談話削弱了這些抑制油價的因素。西德州原油期貨上漲2.51%，收在每桶$88.70，但西德州與布蘭特油價仍均低於一週前。

庫存數據一度抑制油價漲勢。截至11月6日當週，美國原油庫存增加465.7萬桶，市場原估減少148.3萬桶，前值則減少86.5萬桶。蒸餾油庫存增加407.1萬桶，原估減少87萬桶；汽油庫存增加179.9萬桶，原估減少35萬桶。Bloomberg指出，美國原油累庫的部分原因，是高昂運費與中東出口恢復，使美國煉油商得以買進較便宜的原油。實體庫存增加與外交風險再起，在盤中對油價形成相反作用。

Hammack這次不僅說明為何要升息，也談到升息方式。她在10月會議曾投下異議票，主張升息0.25個百分點；如今認為通膨朝2%目標下降的進展已停滯，最新數據更朝錯誤方向移動。她偏好穩定、小幅升息，讓家庭與企業較容易調整。若聯準會落後形勢，她願考慮更強力行動，但認為目前尚未如此，對12月會議仍保持開放態度。

今年沒有投票權的Daly則表示，價格壓力已超出直接受到關稅或油價影響最大的產業。她在史丹佛大學表示，聽到更多企業考慮把投入成本轉嫁給客戶。她仍支持9月升息與10月暫停，但傾向進一步緊縮。至於AI，她認為相關建設確實推高部分價格，但漲幅有限、擴散範圍也不廣，目前對整體通膨的影響仍小。她看好最終的生產力效益，但無法確定何時顯現。

聯準會理事Michael Barr在耶魯大學提出另一角度：AI投資已支撐需求，推升半導體、運算設備與營建勞工價格，整體生產力的提升可能較晚才出現。他警告，短期就業可能遭受嚴重衝擊，尤其是年輕、經驗較少的勞工，但這項技術也可能創造新工作，並與既有工作相輔相成。他認為，不同結果取決於技術取得機會與市場集中程度，未表明利率立場。路透將他強調短期成本的觀點，與主席Kevin Warsh著重生產力可能降低通膨的看法作比較。

週四公布的勞動與房市數據，呈現既有緊縮政策不均衡的影響。截至11月7日當週，初領失業救濟人數增加9,000人至20萬人，高於市場預估的19.5萬人。截至10月31日當週，續領人數減少2萬人至169.7萬人，低於預估的171萬人。裁員仍少，但路透報導指出，企業留住員工不等於積極招聘。Pantheon Macroeconomics的Olivia Cross預期第4季裁員仍有限，同時認為金融條件收緊與AI採用增加，可能在2027年帶來壓力。花旗的Veronica Clark則指出，退休與移民限制也可能縮小潛在申領人口。

房市疲弱更為明顯。10月成屋銷售下降5.5%，年率降至375萬戶，低於預估的385萬戶，前值為397萬戶。全美不動產經紀人協會（NAR）公布的數據顯示，交易活動降至16年低點。西部銷售創1999年有紀錄以來最低，南部與中西部也降至十多年來最弱；公寓銷售同樣創1999年開始統計以來新低。

需求轉弱伴隨供給增加與房價漲幅放緩。待售成屋庫存年增4.6%至159萬戶，相當於5.1個月銷售量，為2015年底以來最高。房價中位數年增僅0.4%至$416,700，是2月以來最小漲幅。NAR經濟學家Lawrence Yun認為，房貸利率若下降，可能釋放遞延需求。目前逾7%的房貸利率，以及降至2025年中以來最弱的購屋負擔能力指標，仍壓抑成交。

美國財政部$250億30年期公債標售，得標殖利率為5.441%，前次為5.618%；投標倍數由2.54降至2.36，21.29%的配售量落在最高得標殖利率。市場正適應更高的預期政策利率路徑，這次標售也增加了長天期公債供給。其他資產方面，美元指數上漲0.25%至103.172，黃金期貨下跌2.97%至每盎司$3,881.70。標普500下跌0.35%，那斯達克100下跌0.30%，當日債市走弱之際，整體股市跌幅相對有限。

## Nvidia換帥考驗AI融資模式

美國交易時段，Nvidia領導層危機從董事會商議發展到黃仁勳遭撤換。此前有報導揭露其婚外情，其中一名女性被美國官員懷疑為中國從事間諜活動。財務長Colette Kress接任代理執行長，公司開始尋找正式接班人。Nvidia股價一度下跌14%，終場跌4.3%；競爭對手Broadcom與超微則因可能取得更多業務的預期，雙雙上漲逾5%。

信用違約保護成本走勢不同。根據ICE Data Services，Nvidia的5年期CDS先升後降，截至紐約時間下午1時30分，下跌2.25個基點至139個基點。交易員認為，黃仁勳離任可能使公司減少借款，以及對其他AI企業的財務支持。其他晶片商與超大規模雲端業者的保護成本也下降，反映市場預期它們可能取得更多業務，或未來借款放慢。不過，Nvidia的CDS仍超過6月初的三倍，顯示換帥之前，市場已大幅重估其信用風險。

Nvidia融資平台的新報導，具體呈現新管理團隊面臨的問題。知情人士向Bloomberg表示，公司宣布與六家資產管理機構合作建立$5,000億平台至今已數月，尚未促成任何交易。過去一個月，客戶與合作夥伴持續要求提高晶片殘值支持，超過原擬每筆交易25%的上限。最快可能到1月才有公告，且須視這次領導層動盪後，個別交易與整體計畫能否維持。

融資工具仰賴約定的運算容量付款，以及晶片剩餘價值，因此供應商提供多少保障相當重要。保障提高可改善評等、降低客戶借款成本，但也將更多風險轉由供應商承擔。Nvidia的合作夥伴為Apollo、BlackRock、Blackstone、Brookfield、Goldman Sachs與KKR。這項已宣布、規模達$5,000億的融資構想，落實過程困難，如今由代理管理團隊領導的公司接手協商。

Broadcom是最直接的競爭對照。5月一筆涉及Anthropic租用晶片、總額$350億的交易中，Broadcom提供$300億保障，協助獲支持的部分取得投資級評等。第二筆Anthropic融資規模$630億，Broadcom保障比例達72.5%，約$430億。美國銀行、花旗與摩根士丹利安排第一順位擔保融資；Blackstone則是已承諾第二順位擔保融資的唯一提供者，部分融資預計第1季分銷予更廣泛的貸款機構。這些較高的保障比例，有助解釋為何Nvidia擬提供的25%支持成為協商焦點。

富國銀行全球高評級債券承銷主管Maureen O'Connor指出，傳統投資級發債也面臨投資人承接能力限制。規模超過約$250億的交易，已在次級市場遭遇阻力，投資人也開始抗拒過密的發行頻率。今年五大超大規模雲端業者發債已超過$2,000億；若納入Nvidia、SpaceX等企業相關資料中心交易，總額約$4,000億。她預期明年會出現更多資產負債表外晶片融資，加權平均年限通常約3年，相較之下，今年AI債券的平均到期年限約15年。

Alphabet則顯示，其他投資人群體仍可提供資金。公司首次發行港幣與新加坡幣債券，合計完成近$40億等值融資。港幣160億元發行涵蓋2年、5年與10年期；新加坡幣22.8億元交易除上述年期外，另有30年期。港幣債定價較初步討論收緊25至30個基點，最終指引時訂單超過港幣325億元；新加坡幣債定價改善20至25個基點，需求超過新加坡幣40億元。資金供一般企業用途，也可能償還債務。

Natixis經濟學家Gary Ng認為，亞洲本幣市場較不擁擠，而且投資人難得能以本國貨幣買進高評級全球科技公司的債券，因此具有吸引力。這些已完成的發行，將Alphabet先前的洽談轉為實際資金；同時，AI相關波動也使市場更仔細檢視產業借款。

假期後，CoreWeave週二公布財報後的首波現券反應浮現。其2031年到期、票息9.75%的債券，週四上午每1美元面額上漲約0.3美分至82.25美分，信用違約保護成本降幅也位居CDX高收益指數成分企業前列。公司股價則在週三上漲約25%後，下跌約7.6%。債權人與股東對同一份財報的反應，反映各自在企業中的權利不同。

公司擬籌措至少$40億貸款，如今結構細節更清楚：透過獨立實體發行，以Meta合約為支持，相關GPU及其他資產提供擔保，期限六年並有部分攤還。CoreWeave本身仍屬投機級，但Meta的信用狀況預期可協助貸款取得投資級評等。摩根士丹利與三菱日聯正考慮最快本週開始分階段聯貸，早於先前預期。管理層初步討論的殖利率為7%至7.5%；相較之下，CoreWeave另一筆2032年到期非投資級債券，週四上午10時08分價格為81美分，殖利率達14.5%。

其他企業的再融資成本依然高昂。Internet Brands恢復與投資人洽談約$35億融資，包括最多$20億槓桿貸款，以及約$15億首次發行的高收益債。初步債券殖利率討論由至少10.5%提高至約11%。加拿大皇家銀行主導前期行銷，可能下週正式推出。這家KKR支持、持有WebMD的企業，曾因利率上升與發行擁擠而延後9月交易；公司約$30億第一順位擔保貸款將於2028年5月到期，另有$28億貸款，包括循環額度，於2029至2031年到期。

電力需求使融資機會從晶片擴大至其他領域。花旗永續長Valerie Smith表示，電氣化正協助銀行朝2030年$1兆永續金融目標推進，目前已完成約$6,470億，合資格範圍如今也納入核能與以自然為本的解決方案。淡馬錫的Kyung-Ah Park則指出，電網與變壓器供應是主要瓶頸。這些觀察顯示，AI建設所需資本，除運算設備外也涵蓋發電與電網。

## 日本通膨與匯率壓力交織，全球成長冷熱不均

日本10月企業物價指數年增7.1%，高於預估的6.5%，也較前值6.8%加速；月增0.7%，為5月以來最快。上游壓力擴大的細項包括，石油與煤製品年增率由11.5%升至15.9%，化學品由13.4%升至15.5%，運輸設備由2.9%升至3.2%；日圓計價進口物價年增24.8%。

日本央行物價統計官員Sayaka Yamazaki表示，企業正轉嫁勞工與原料成本，會計年度下半年開始也影響調價。路透指出，運輸設備漲價的部分原因，是AI需求帶動半導體成本。這份數據強化緊縮理由之際，日圓也正逼近已引起官方關注的價位。

9月反對升息的央行審議委員Toichiro Asada週四表示，對漸進升息持開放態度，但希望步調謹慎。他接受基礎通膨已符合央行目標，也未主張降息；疑慮在於，近期漲價未必由需求帶動，民間消費疲弱，經濟容易受到過度緊縮傷害。他的立場容許再次升息，但對速度與需求條件仍有實質保留。

其後日圓自9月以來首次跌破每美元160日圓，隨後回升至159.88，當日貶幅不到0.1%。日本財務官三村淳表示，近期匯率變動過快，並提及先前干預。官員持續強調變動速度與失序程度，未設定固定觸發價位。道明證券Howard Du認為，近期干預風險偏低，理由是市場對官方先前行動仍記憶猶新，而美國實質利率上升也支撐美元兌日圓。

最新報導量化了為何日本殖利率上升，未直接帶來日圓回升。1至10月，外資買進日本債券與股票合計創紀錄達日圓34.5兆元；日本投資人今年則淨賣出日圓6,890億元海外證券，去年為買進日圓12.5兆元。然而，日本企業對外直接投資扣除盈餘再投資後仍達日圓11.9兆元。花旗策略師也指出，外資股票買家會賣出日圓避險。日本持有的海外證券資產達日圓811兆元，持續對外直接投資，使跨境資金流仍然龐大，即使部分證券投資資金回流亦然。

紐西蘭則呈現強勁的公債需求。週四2037年4月到期公債標售，投標倍數達7.46，為2013年2月以來所有年期最高。10年期殖利率延續跌勢，下降4個基點至4.64%。ITC Markets的Kit Lowe認為，初步選舉結果減輕財政疑慮、每週發行量由紐幣4.5億元降至3.5億元，以及大筆票息發放後的再投資需求，共同提供支撐。

英國成長轉強，但動能集中。第3季GDP季增0.7%，符合預期，高於第2季的0.5%。9月月增0.2%，優於原估持平；8月則由增長0.1%下修為零。服務業第3季成長0.9%，由電腦程式設計與相關活動領軍；生產部門增長0.1%，營建業則萎縮0.7%。企業投資僅增0.4%，約為預期增幅的一半。科技活動拉高整體成長，但更廣泛的投資表現較欠說服力。

RICS房市調查則反映融資成本偏高的另一面。10月對未來一年銷售的預期指標降至負17，為2023年7月以來最低，受訪者預期房價將下跌1%。房貸利率約6%，高於伊朗衝突前的4.83%，壓抑需求。成長與房市數據，讓英國央行對不同產業韌性收到明顯不同的訊號。Bloomberg當日市場報導顯示，英國10年期公債殖利率上升8個基點至5.30%。

路透最新歐洲央行調查中，71名經濟學家一致預期12月升息0.25個百分點至2.75%。分歧在於緊縮終點：46人認為2.75%就是終點利率，25人預期至少再升息一次，最可能在2027年第1季。市場定價則顯示，至2027年底還會升息約兩至三次，比預測中位數更緊。經濟學家將2027年通膨預測由2.6%調高至2.8%，成長預測由1.2%調高至1.3%。

Wellington的Fabio Balboni認為，3月是否再升息取決於基礎通膨是否持續，並指出勞工要求調薪彌補購買力損失的風險。Nordea的Jan von Gerich警告，天然氣儲量偏低之際，油期貨下跌可能掩蓋冬季能源風險。歐洲央行接班協商也未定案：德國明確否認《觀點》雜誌所稱，梅爾茨與馬克宏已同意支持Pablo Hernandez de Cos接替拉加德的報導。

## 財政選擇拉開主權融資差異

美國2027會計年度首月，10月赤字創紀錄達$4,040億，較去年同期增加42%。收入下降9%至$3,690億，支出增加12%至$7,730億。即使調整福利給付時點，赤字仍達$2,850億，增加$940億或49%，顯示財政惡化超出日曆因素。

關稅收入下降39%至$192億，個人非扣繳所得稅下降36%至$510億。後者部分受到比較基期扭曲：加州野火相關報稅展延，曾推高2025年10月收入。農業支出增加$140億，包含農業紓困；軍事支出增加$280億，部分因前一年政府停擺，使軍方信託基金付款延後。利息支出總額增加11%至$1,150億。財政部預估全年赤字約$2.2兆，高於前一會計年度的$1.99兆，在當日殖利率走高之際，融資需求仍然龐大。

巴西的新進展，是可能將2027年財政調整擴大至約800億雷亞爾，約合$142億。討論中的追加措施，將限制強制性支出與目前不計入財政目標的支出，補充已提交的500億至600億雷亞爾方案。政府希望年底前向國會提交修憲案。消息傳出後，雷亞爾一度縮小跌幅，交換利率也收斂升幅。不過，魯拉所屬政黨內部有反彈，政府也持續迴避停止基本工資實質調升，因此追加措施的範圍與能否通過仍不確定。

波蘭公債正反映更明顯的財政溢價。Bloomberg最新分析指出，10年期殖利率達6.2%，今年上升約100個基點，與利率交換的差距擴至至少16年來最大。為支應約GDP 7%的赤字，債務發行量自2023年以來幾乎倍增，最高每月達$100億。PGIM的Magdalena Polan認為，償債成本正轉向更高水準，並質疑在政治兩極化下，能否實現有意義的財政整頓。

投資人對此看法不一。Aviva的Kurt Knowlson認為，制度、經濟韌性與歐盟資金仍提供支撐；William Blair的Daniel Wood則認為，債券市場可能高估政治風險。波蘭主權評等仍屬投資級，市場疑慮集中在財政走向及政治體系改變走向的能力；投資組合轉向匈牙利，也呈現區域內的差異。

哥倫比亞銀行業者指出，主權殖利率直接推升民間借款成本。Grupo Aval的Maria Lorena Gutierrez表示，TES公債殖利率為銀行存款成本設定下限，壓縮利差並提高放款利率。Davivienda的Javier Suarez指出，房貸利率達14%至15%，18個月前業界平均僅11.9%。政府預算顯示，若不調整，赤字可能超過GDP 9%，因此正爭取通過可在明年削減逾GDP 2個百分點赤字的法案。銀行高層支持方案的迫切性，包括延長銀行業5%附加稅的提議，但對長期負擔仍有異議。

迦納預算一方面擬提前還款，一方面降低初級盈餘目標。財長Cassiel Ato Forson計畫在12月31日前，支付1月2日到期的$5.9億歐洲債券款項，以及2月的國內債務。為支應四年$100億成長計畫，政府擬自2027年將初級盈餘目標由GDP 1.5%降至0.5%，並將收入與補助由今年預估的GDP 17.2%提高至18.1%。整體赤字預估由2%擴至明年的2.9%。政府以2030年成長8%為目標，2027年則預估5.2%。

斯里蘭卡2027年預算同樣希望在維持財政整頓之餘擴大投資。總統Anura Kumara Dissanayake提議減少經常支出、增加資本投資，並在中期將赤字降至GDP 5%以下。政府正研擬投資保護法，也在現行$30億IMF安排即將結束之際，評估是否需要另一項計畫。若達成工作人員層級協議，可望取得約$3.45億資金。這些財政與融資規畫，發生在復甦仍脆弱之際。

印尼匯債市場呈現殖利率吸引力與信心之間的拉扯。印尼盾一度貶值0.5%，創每美元18,241印尼盾新低，促使印尼央行干預即期與遠期市場，並在次級市場買進公債。10年期殖利率上升4個基點至7.66%。然而，外資11月仍流入債市$1.74億，週二標售的外資參與比例也由前次8.5%升至22.6%。這些流入，與MSCI重新分類疑慮及副總統Gibran Rakabuming Raka辭職後的政治不確定性並存。

越南官員認為借款成本過高，因而延後國際發債。財長Ngo Van Tuan表示，將持續準備並與投資人接觸，等待更好條件；先前討論的主權美元債規模最高$10億。塞爾維亞則立即採取政策行動，意外升息0.25個百分點至6%，打破市場一致預期的按兵不動。央行指出能源成本轉嫁與匯率壓力，10月通膨也由4.1%加速至4.4%。土耳其則把2027年底通膨預測與目標由15%上調至21%；總裁Fatih Karahan表示，這項調整不改變政策，10月利率已降至36%。

## 債權回收價值與永續資本面臨新考驗

Citgo最新獲利與現金展望，讓市場更加揣測Elliott支持的Amber Energy原擬$59億收購案可能重新檢討。煉油商Citgo預期年底現金最高達$70億，全年EBITDA最高$75億，高於先前預估的$58億。油價上漲帶來的額外收益，大幅提高這筆原本用來清償$88億債權的出售交易所涉及資產價值。

部分Citgo相關債券每1美元面額最高成交至120美分，比收購協議所對應價值高約6%。這批2020年到期債券以母公司50.1%股權擔保。巴克萊先前估計，若交易6月完成，簽署協議者每單位本金可獲支付$128，其他持有人為$108；每延後一個月，付款增加0.75%。兩組債券市價差距縮小，反映市場預期條件可能重新考量。

法律效力與最終回收額仍是不同問題。上訴法院10月確認債券有效，但委內瑞拉等方面仍就選擇Amber出價提出上訴。Caledonia交易員Francesco Marani表示，若出售失敗，持有人可能爭取原始請求權，估計相當於每1美元面額170至180美分，但也強調和解金額未必等同該數字。營運價值上升提高債權人協商期待，最終分配仍未確定。

一份新公開的KPMG查核報告，釐清委內瑞拉另一部分財務狀況。2026年前九個月，超過$121億石油與天然氣收入流經美國財政部管理的帳戶；存入資金近99%、即$121.1億已撥付。多數款項透過委內瑞拉外匯拍賣支付，另約$1.33億直接付給政府供應商。報告認定資金屬委內瑞拉主權財產，允許用途受國務卿Marco Rubio行使的權限約束。

SAS則面臨債權是否存續的爭議。持有瑞士法郎1.272億元次順位永續債逾半數的持有人主張，航空公司的美國《破產法》第11章重整未在瑞士獲承認。這批債券自2023年1月以來未付年度利息；持有人在11月5日函件中要求執行債權，並主張發行人SAS Consortium未納入同步進行的瑞典重整。SAS確認收到函件並正審視；其重整原本將這批債券視為已註銷、回收為零。爭議可能使法航荷航擬提高持股至60.5%、取得控制權的計畫更複雜。

針對美國銀行$220億永久固定票息特別股的新研究，凸顯另一種期限延長風險。今年這類證券總報酬下跌8.5%，平均價格約為每1美元面額61美分。由於以新融資取代票息低於5%的特別股將增加成本，發行人未行使可用的贖回權。摩根士丹利一筆$13億、1月可贖回的發行，參考價為61.4美分；U.S. Bancorp票息3.75%的系列則約55美分。票息依契約永久固定，發行人贖回是否划算，成為價格回升前景的關鍵；今年新發行的永久固定票息特別股平均票息為6.69%。

德國央行另警告，若利率上升，或基金因贖回被迫出售，商用不動產價格可能再跌。該行指出，2024年以來的復甦僅涉及相對少量交易，且集中在較優質建物，辦公與零售物業價格最近已略降。8月不動產基金占德國共同基金資產13%，低於2023年底的21%。多檔基金限制提款，顯示流動性更緊；貸款機構Deutsche Pfandbriefbank也預期，近期環境不會改善。

## 後續市場焦點

美債下跌與油價反彈後，週五美國生產者物價數據將提供下一個上游通膨觀察點。能源成本、科技相關投入與更廣泛價格壓力之間的差別，對12月政策辯論仍重要。Hammack主張更頻繁的常規幅度升息，只有在聯準會落後形勢時才考慮更強行動；Daly的企業訪談則顯示，更廣泛的成本轉嫁正被考慮。下一份物價數據公布前，期貨已反映12月、1月與3月各升息0.25個百分點。

日本週一GDP將在12月17至18日央行會議前，檢驗Asada所擔憂的需求面。經濟學家預期消費支出將近兩年來首次下降。這項數據、10月生產者物價加速，以及日圓接近每美元160的組合，將影響進口成本壓力與國內支出之間的政策權衡。再度干預仍是獨立的匯率風險，官方關注的是走勢性質，未宣布固定匯價觸發點。

Nvidia的11月17日財報，是代理領導團隊上任後首個重大財務考驗，也將面對未來供應商支持與延宕融資平台的問題。Anthropic發行案及CoreWeave擬議的擔保聯貸，則將各自檢驗機構需求能否轉為條件可接受的實際融資。Nvidia先前承諾買進約$100億Anthropic股份；黃仁勳離任後，這項具體承諾仍受到關注。

財政決策也有各自期限。巴西計畫年底前提出修憲案；哥倫比亞須在今年通過救援法案，才能使措施於2027年初生效。迦納計畫12月31日付款，將檢驗提前還款承諾能否落實。歐盟執委會擬在11月26至27日歐洲理事會會議前，提出烏克蘭2027年融資提案與新一輪俄羅斯制裁；融資工具與負擔分攤仍在討論。

石油外交與航運安全，仍可能在既定數據之外改變通膨展望。美國庫存大增改善了當下國內庫存狀況，川普更強硬的立場則降低市場對談判解決的信心。進入下一個亞洲交易時段，區域供應恢復能否持續、外交若有進展將採取何種條件，仍未明朗。

overall_summary.headline: 油價與升息主張扭轉早盤避險買盤，美債下跌
overall_summary.session_narrative:
油價反彈，聯準會官員強化進一步緊縮的理由，美國公債扭轉Nvidia領導層危機帶來的早盤避險漲勢。2年期殖利率上升14.37個基點至4.8814%，10年期上升13.75個基點至5.1271%；2年與10年期利差收窄0.62個基點至24.57個基點。10年期升幅主要來自實質借款成本提高：抗通膨公債殖利率上升9.59個基點，通膨補償上升4.16個基點。

川普表示美國可以不與伊朗達成協議，削弱外交樂觀情緒，即使美國庫存大增，仍推升油價。克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack主張更頻繁、小幅升息；舊金山聯準銀行總裁Mary Daly認為，企業正考慮轉嫁成本，可能仍須進一步緊縮。裁員偏低、成屋銷售大幅轉弱，呈現既有緊縮政策不均衡的影響，12月升息幅度仍有分歧。

Nvidia撤換黃仁勳，由Colette Kress暫代執行長。交易員評估這次交接是否會使公司減少借款及對其他AI企業的支持，信用違約保護成本先升後降。公司宣布的$5,000億融資平台仍未促成交易，合作夥伴要求將殘值支持提高至原擬25%上限以上。Alphabet仍完成近$40億等值的亞洲本幣借款，CoreWeave也因擔保融資條款更明確而帶動債券走強。投資人的承接能力，以及供應商支持的融資能否落實，仍是主要不確定性。
overall_summary.summary: 美債重估主要由實質殖利率上升帶動，通膨補償也增加。Nvidia換帥使供應商支持的AI融資浮現疑問，同時Alphabet完成亞洲借款，CoreWeave債券也走強。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries sold off as a rebound in oil and renewed Federal Reserve calls for tighter policy overwhelmed an early haven bid linked to Nvidia's leadership crisis. The two-year yield rose 14.37 basis points to 4.8814%, while the 10-year climbed 13.75 basis points to 5.1271%. Trading resumed after the Veterans Day closure with inflation and the expected pace of rate increases exerting more influence on bonds than the decline in technology shares.

President Donald Trump's assertion that the U.S. could forgo an agreement with Iran reversed some of the optimism surrounding diplomacy. Brent futures rose 3.24% to $95.77 a barrel, even as U.S. inventories showed substantial increases in crude and refined products. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack favored more frequent, smaller increases, while San Francisco's Mary Daly said further tightening would probably be necessary as businesses considered passing on higher costs. Their remarks reinforced the direction of policy while leaving the size of December's move contested.

Credit markets distinguished between equity disruption and borrowers' financing prospects. Nvidia removed Jensen Huang and installed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO, but its default-protection costs declined after an initial rise. Alphabet completed almost $4 billion-equivalent of Asian local-currency borrowing, and CoreWeave's bonds improved as investors assessed more detailed plans for secured financing. Those transactions and price responses unfolded alongside fresh warnings about the capacity of bond investors to absorb the AI industry's continuing demand for capital.

## Oil and Fed Tightening Overturn the Early Treasury Bid

Long-duration Treasuries initially benefited from uncertainty surrounding Nvidia. During the early reopening, the 30-year yield fell as much as 3 basis points to 5.32%, and the 10-year steadied around 4.99%. Commonwealth Bank of Australia's Carol Kong attributed the modest haven demand to concern about the company at the center of the AI investment boom. The shorter end was already under pressure from inflation and expectations for additional Fed increases.

That early support gave way as energy prices rose and policymakers reinforced the case for restraint. By the close, the five-year yield was 15.11 basis points higher at 4.9704%, the largest increase among the principal coupon maturities, while the 30-year rose 9.97 basis points to 5.4521%. The two- to 10-year spread narrowed 0.62 basis point to 24.57 basis points; the two- to 30-year gap contracted 4.4 basis points to 57.07 basis points. The market continued to compress the extra yield available for extending beyond policy-sensitive maturities.

The weekly comparison shows the concentration of that adjustment. Two-year yields were up 41.91 basis points, against 29.24 basis points at 10 years and 19.82 basis points at 30 years. Over a month, the two-year was 9.45 basis points higher, while the 10- and 30-year yields remained 11.07 and 14.35 basis points lower. The sharp recent repricing of the policy path has therefore coexisted with some remaining gains in longer bonds over the broader period.

Higher real borrowing costs accounted for most of Thursday's 10-year increase, with inflation compensation also rising. The 10-year TIPS yield climbed 9.59 basis points to 2.8662%, and the breakeven rose 4.16 basis points to 2.2609%. Over the week, real yields increased 26.85 basis points, compared with a 2.39-basis-point rise in the breakeven. The oil rebound added an inflation component to a selloff still dominated by higher real yields.

Trump said Washington did not need an Iran agreement and directed Vice President JD Vance toward domestic issues. Crude had previously weakened on signs of recovering Middle East supply and hopes for a diplomatic resolution. His remarks reduced that support. WTI futures finished at $88.70 a barrel, up 2.51%, although both WTI and Brent remained below their week-earlier levels.

The inventory release briefly checked the rally. For the week ended November 6, U.S. crude stocks increased 4.657 million barrels against an expected 1.483 million-barrel decline and a previous 0.865 million-barrel draw. Distillate inventories rose 4.071 million barrels, compared with an expected 0.87 million-barrel decline, while gasoline stocks increased 1.799 million against a forecast 0.35 million-barrel draw. Bloomberg attributed the accumulation of U.S. crude partly to high shipping costs and recovering Middle East exports, which left domestic refiners able to purchase cheaper barrels. The physical-stock increase and the renewed diplomatic risk pulled oil in different directions during the session.

Hammack's fresh remarks concerned how to tighten as well as why. The Cleveland president, who dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase at October's meeting, said progress toward 2% inflation had stalled and the latest data were moving the wrong way. She preferred steady, smaller increases because households and businesses could adjust more easily than to sharper moves. She would consider stronger action if the Fed fell behind, but did not judge that to be the current position and would approach December with an open mind.

Daly, a nonvoter this year, separately said pressure extended beyond sectors most directly affected by tariffs or oil. At Stanford, she reported hearing more businesses contemplate passing input costs to customers. She continued to support September's increase and October's pause, but her bias was toward further tightening. She also differentiated the AI contribution: the buildout was raising some prices, yet its present effect on overall inflation remained modest because those increases were not large or spreading widely. She remained optimistic about eventual productivity benefits while uncertain about their timing.

Governor Michael Barr supplied a distinct assessment at Yale. AI investment was already supporting demand and increasing prices for semiconductors, computing equipment and construction labor, he said, while aggregate productivity gains could take longer to emerge. He warned of potentially serious short-term employment disruption, particularly for younger and less-experienced workers, alongside the possibility of new jobs and complementary uses of the technology. His speech offered competing outcomes depending on access and market concentration, without specifying a rate preference. Reuters contrasted his emphasis on near-term costs with Chair Kevin Warsh's emphasis on potential disinflation from productivity.

Thursday's labor and housing releases showed the uneven effects of existing restraint. Initial unemployment claims increased 9,000 to 200,000 for the week ended November 7, above the 195,000 consensus. Continuing claims fell 20,000 to 1.697 million for the week ended October 31, below the expected 1.710 million. Layoffs remained low, but Reuters' reporting distinguished employee retention from strong hiring. Pantheon Macroeconomics' Olivia Cross expected limited layoffs through Q4 while identifying tighter financial conditions and greater AI adoption as possible pressures in 2027. Citi's Veronica Clark said retirement and immigration restrictions could also be reducing the pool of potential claimants.

Housing showed much greater weakness. October existing-home sales fell 5.5% to a 3.75 million annual rate, below the 3.85 million consensus and down from 3.97 million. The National Association of Realtors' release put activity at a 16-year low. Sales in the West reached their lowest level in records beginning in 1999; the South and Midwest recorded their weakest results in more than a decade. Condominium sales also fell to a record low in the series beginning in 1999.

More supply and slower price growth were accompanying the loss of demand. Resale inventory increased 4.6% annually to 1.59 million homes, equivalent to 5.1 months of sales, the highest ratio since late 2015. The median price rose only 0.4% to $416,700, its smallest annual gain since February. NAR economist Lawrence Yun saw potential pent-up demand if mortgage rates declined. For now, rates above 7% and an affordability measure at its weakest since mid-2025 were restraining completed transactions.

Treasury's $25 billion 30-year auction cleared at 5.441%, compared with 5.618% at the previous sale. Bid-to-cover declined to 2.36 from 2.54, and 21.29% was allotted at the high yield. The auction added duration as the market adjusted to a higher expected policy path. Across other assets, the Dollar Index gained 0.25% to 103.172 and gold futures fell 2.97% to $3,881.70 an ounce. The S&P 500 lost 0.35% and the Nasdaq 100 0.30%, leaving the day's bond losses alongside a relatively contained decline in broad equities.

## Nvidia's Transition Tests the AI Financing Model

Nvidia's leadership crisis moved from board deliberations to Huang's removal during the U.S. session. Kress became interim CEO as the company began searching for a permanent replacement following reports of affairs, including one with a woman suspected by U.S. officials of spying for China. Nvidia shares fell as much as 14% before finishing 4.3% lower, while rivals Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices gained more than 5% on expectations they could capture business.

Debt protection moved differently. Nvidia's five-year CDS initially rose, then declined 2.25 basis points to 139 basis points by 1:30 p.m. New York time, according to ICE Data Services. Traders cited the possibility that Huang's departure would curb borrowing and financial support for other AI companies. Protection costs on other chipmakers and hyperscalers also fell on expectations of business gains or slower future borrowing. Nvidia's CDS remained more than three times its early-June level, reflecting the substantial reassessment that preceded the leadership change.

New reporting on Nvidia's financing platform gave substance to the questions facing its next management team. Months after the company announced a $500 billion partnership with six asset managers, no deals had resulted, people familiar with negotiations told Bloomberg. Customers and partners had been pressing it during the past month to increase residual-value support beyond the proposed ceiling of 25% of a deal. The earliest likely announcement was January, conditional on the leadership upheaval leaving transactions and the broader project intact.

The support matters because financing vehicles rely on both contracted payments for computing capacity and the residual value of the chips. A larger supplier backstop can improve ratings and reduce borrowing costs for customers, while transferring more risk to the supplier. Nvidia's partners are Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR. The $500 billion platform is an announced financing ambition whose execution has proved difficult, with negotiations now passing to a company under interim leadership.

Broadcom provides the immediate competitive comparison. It backed $30 billion of a $35 billion May transaction involving chips leased by Anthropic, helping supported portions secure investment-grade ratings. A second, $63 billion financing for Anthropic includes a Broadcom backstop covering 72.5%, or about $43 billion. Bank of America, Citi and Morgan Stanley are arranging the first-lien portion; Blackstone is the sole provider of the committed second-lien financing. Portions are expected to be distributed to a wider lender group in Q1. Those support levels help explain why Nvidia's prospective 25% protection has been a point of negotiation.

Wells Fargo's Maureen O'Connor described another constraint: investor capacity for conventional investment-grade issuance. The bank's global head of high-grade syndicate said deals exceeding about $25 billion were meeting secondary-market resistance and that investors were pushing back on issuance frequency. The five largest hyperscalers had already sold more than $200 billion of bonds this year; including data-center deals associated with companies such as Nvidia and SpaceX took volume to about $400 billion. She expected more off-balance-sheet chip financing next year, often with weighted-average lives near three years, against roughly 15-year average maturities on this year's AI bonds.

Alphabet demonstrated continuing access to alternative investor pools. It completed inaugural Hong Kong- and Singapore-dollar offerings totaling almost $4 billion-equivalent. The HK$16 billion issue comprised two-, five- and 10-year maturities; the S$2.28 billion transaction added a 30-year tranche to those maturities. Hong Kong-dollar pricing tightened 25-30 basis points from initial discussions, with orders above HK$32.5 billion at final guidance. Singapore-dollar pricing improved 20-25 basis points, with demand above S$4 billion. Proceeds are for general corporate purposes, potentially including debt repayment.

Natixis economist Gary Ng attributed the attraction to less-crowded Asian local-currency markets and the unusual opportunity to buy a highly rated global technology borrower in investors' home currencies. The completed sales convert Alphabet's earlier discussions into funding, even while AI-related volatility has increased scrutiny of the sector's borrowing.

CoreWeave's first cash-bond response after Tuesday's earnings also became visible following the holiday. Its 9.75% notes due 2031 gained about 0.3 cent to 82.25 cents Thursday morning, and default-protection costs were among the largest decliners in the CDX high-yield index. The company's shares fell about 7.6% after Wednesday's roughly 25% gain. Creditors and shareholders were absorbing the same earnings news through different claims on the business.

The proposed loan of at least $4 billion now has more specific structural terms. It would be backed by a Meta contract, issued through a separate entity, secured by the relevant GPUs and other assets, and mature in six years with some amortization. Meta's credit profile is expected to support an investment-grade rating for the facility even though CoreWeave remains speculative grade. Morgan Stanley and MUFG were considering starting phased syndication as soon as this week, earlier than previously expected. Management's preliminary 7%-7.5% yield discussion contrasts with the 14.5% yield on CoreWeave's separate 2032 junk bonds at 10:08 a.m. Thursday, when those notes traded at 81 cents.

Elsewhere, the cost of refinancing remained demanding. Internet Brands resumed investor discussions for roughly $3.5 billion, comprising a leveraged loan of up to $2 billion and about $1.5 billion of first-time high-yield notes. Early bond-yield discussions increased to around 11% from at least 10.5%. RBC is leading premarketing for a possible launch next week. The KKR-backed owner of WebMD had deferred a September transaction amid higher rates and crowded issuance; it has about $3 billion of first-lien loans due in May 2028 and another $2.8 billion of loans, including a revolver, maturing in 2029-2031.

Power demand is widening the financing opportunity beyond chips. Citi sustainability chief Valerie Smith said electrification was helping drive progress toward the bank's $1 trillion sustainable-finance goal for 2030, with about $647 billion achieved. Its eligibility criteria now include nuclear energy and nature-based solutions. Temasek's Kyung-Ah Park identified electricity grids and transformer supply as major bottlenecks. Those comments place generation and networks alongside computing equipment in the capital requirements created by the buildout.

## Japan's Inflation and Currency Pressure Meet Uneven Global Growth

Japan's October Corporate Goods Price Index rose 7.1% annually, exceeding the 6.5% forecast and accelerating from 6.8%. Monthly prices increased 0.7%, the fastest since May. The details showed wider upstream pressure: petroleum and coal products rose 15.9% annually from 11.5%, chemicals increased 15.5% from 13.4%, and transportation equipment rose 3.2% from 2.9%. Yen-denominated import prices increased 24.8%.

BOJ price-statistics official Sayaka Yamazaki said companies were passing on labor and raw-material costs, with the start of the fiscal year's second half also influencing price revisions. Reuters linked part of the transportation-equipment increase to semiconductor costs associated with AI demand. The release strengthened the tightening argument while the currency was approaching a level already attracting official attention.

Board member Toichiro Asada, who opposed September's increase, said Thursday that he was open to gradual hikes but wanted caution over their pace. He accepted that underlying inflation was consistent with the BOJ's target and did not seek a rate cut. His concern was that recent price increases were not necessarily demand-driven and that weak private consumption made the economy vulnerable to excessive restraint. His position leaves room for another increase while preserving a substantive disagreement about speed and demand conditions.

The yen subsequently crossed 160 per dollar for the first time since September before recovering to 159.88, down less than 0.1% on the session. Currency chief Atsushi Mimura said recent moves had been too fast and recalled earlier intervention. Officials continued to emphasize speed and disorderliness over a fixed trigger. TD Securities' Howard Du considered near-term intervention risk low, citing the fresh memory of official action and the rise in U.S. real rates supporting dollar-yen.

Fresh reporting quantified why higher Japanese yields have not produced a straightforward currency recovery. Foreign investors bought a record combined ¥34.5 trillion of Japanese bonds and equities from January through October, while Japanese investors sold a net ¥689 billion of foreign securities this year after ¥12.5 trillion of purchases last year. Yet Japanese companies invested ¥11.9 trillion abroad through direct investment excluding reinvested earnings. Citi strategists also pointed to foreign equity buyers hedging by selling yen. Japan's ¥811 trillion stock of overseas portfolio assets and continuing direct investment sustain cross-border flows even as some portfolio money returns home.

New Zealand supplied a different demand result. Thursday's April 2037 bond auction attracted bids for 7.46 times the amount offered, the strongest ratio for any tenor since February 2013. The 10-year yield extended its decline to 4.64%, down 4 basis points. ITC Markets' Kit Lowe cited preliminary election results easing fiscal concerns, a reduction in weekly issuance to NZ$350 million from NZ$450 million, and reinvestment demand from large coupon payments.

Britain's growth release was stronger, though concentrated. Q3 GDP rose 0.7%, matching consensus and accelerating from 0.5% in Q2. September's 0.2% monthly expansion beat expectations for no growth, while August was revised down to zero from 0.1%. Services grew 0.9% in the quarter, led by computer programming and related activities; production increased 0.1%, but construction contracted 0.7%. Business investment rose just 0.4%, roughly half the expected increase. Strong technology activity lifted the aggregate while leaving broader investment less convincing.

The RICS housing survey showed a separate consequence of high financing costs. Its October measure of expected sales over the next year fell to minus 17, the weakest since July 2023, and respondents expected prices to decline 1%. Mortgage rates around 6%, against 4.83% before the Iran conflict, were weighing on demand. The growth and housing observations give the BOE materially different signals about resilience across sectors. Britain's 10-year yield rose 8 basis points to 5.30% in Bloomberg's session account.

A new Reuters ECB survey found unanimous expectations among 71 economists for a December quarter-point increase to 2.75%. The disagreement concerned where tightening would end: 46 expected that to be the terminal rate, while 25 expected at least one more increase, most likely in Q1 2027. Market pricing implied roughly two to three further increases through end-2027, a more restrictive path than the median forecast. Economists raised their 2027 inflation forecast to 2.8% from 2.6% and growth to 1.3% from 1.2%.

Wellington's Fabio Balboni made a March increase conditional on persistent underlying inflation and identified wage demands compensating for lost purchasing power as a risk. Nordea's Jan von Gerich warned that lower oil futures could obscure winter energy exposure with gas storage low. ECB leadership negotiations remained unsettled: Germany explicitly denied a Le Point report that Friedrich Merz and Emmanuel Macron had agreed to support Pablo Hernandez de Cos as Christine Lagarde's successor.

## Fiscal Choices Differentiate Sovereign Funding

The U.S. began fiscal 2027 with a record $404 billion October deficit, 42% above the year-earlier shortfall. Receipts fell 9% to $369 billion while outlays increased 12% to $773 billion. Adjusting for benefit-payment shifts still left a $285 billion deficit, up $94 billion, or 49%, demonstrating deterioration beyond the calendar effect.

Customs collections fell 39% to $19.2 billion, while individual non-withheld income taxes dropped 36% to $51 billion. The latter comparison was distorted partly by elevated October 2025 receipts after California wildfire-related filing extensions. Agriculture spending rose $14 billion, including farm relief; military outlays increased $28 billion, partly because payments to military trust funds had been delayed by the previous year's shutdown. Gross interest expense rose 11% to $115 billion. Treasury projected a roughly $2.2 trillion annual deficit, against the previous fiscal year's $1.99 trillion, leaving substantial financing needs alongside the day's higher yields.

Brazil's new development was a prospective expansion of its fiscal adjustment to around 80 billion reais, or $14.2 billion, in 2027. Additional measures under discussion would curb mandatory expenditure and spending currently excluded from fiscal targets, complementing the 50 billion-60 billion reais plan already submitted. The administration aims to send a constitutional amendment to Congress before year-end. The real briefly reduced losses and swap rates pared increases on the news. Resistance within Lula's party and the government's continued avoidance of an end to real minimum-wage increases leave the scope and passage of the additional measures uncertain.

Polish debt is attracting a more explicit fiscal premium. Bloomberg's new assessment put 10-year yields at 6.2%, about 100 basis points higher this year, with the gap over interest-rate swaps at its widest in at least 16 years. Debt issuance has nearly doubled since 2023 to as much as $10 billion a month, financing a deficit around 7% of GDP. PGIM's Magdalena Polan described a shift toward higher servicing costs and questioned the prospects for meaningful consolidation amid political polarization.

The assessment was contested. Aviva's Kurt Knowlson cited institutions, economic resilience and EU funding as anchors, while William Blair's Daniel Wood thought bonds might be overstating political risk. The sovereign remains investment grade. Investors' concern centers on the fiscal trajectory and political capacity to change it, with portfolio shifts toward Hungary illustrating the regional differentiation.

Colombian bankers described a direct channel from sovereign yields to private borrowing. Grupo Aval's Maria Lorena Gutierrez said TES yields set a floor under banks' deposit costs, compressing margins and raising lending rates. Davivienda's Javier Suarez put mortgage rates at 14%-15%, against a sector average of 11.9% 18 months earlier. The government is seeking legislation worth more than 2 percentage points of GDP in deficit reduction next year after a budget showing the deficit could exceed 9% without adjustment. Bank executives supported the package's urgency, including a proposed extension of their industry's 5% surcharge, while disputing its longer-run burden.

Ghana's budget combined proposed early payments with less ambitious primary surpluses. Finance Minister Cassiel Ato Forson plans to settle the $590 million January 2 eurobond payment and February domestic obligation by December 31. A $10 billion four-year growth program would be financed partly by reducing the primary-surplus objective to 0.5% of GDP from 1.5% starting in 2027 and raising revenue and grants to 18.1% from 17.2% projected this year. The overall deficit is forecast to widen to 2.9% next year from 2%. The government targets 8% growth in 2030, compared with 5.2% in 2027.

Sri Lanka's 2027 budget similarly sought more investment while preserving consolidation. President Anura Kumara Dissanayake proposed reducing current expenditure, increasing capital investment and bringing the deficit below 5% of GDP over the medium term. An investment-protection law is being prepared, and the government is assessing whether another IMF program is needed as its $3 billion arrangement approaches its end. A staff-level agreement could unlock about $345 million. These are planned fiscal and financing steps during a still-fragile recovery.

Indonesia's currency and bonds showed the tension between yield appeal and confidence. The rupiah fell as much as 0.5% to a record 18,241 per dollar, prompting Bank Indonesia intervention in spot and forward markets and secondary-market government-bond purchases. The 10-year yield rose 4 basis points to 7.66%. Foreign funds had nevertheless put $174 million into bonds in November, and foreign participation at Tuesday's auction increased to 22.6% from 8.5% at the previous sale. Those inflows coexist with MSCI reclassification concerns and political uncertainty following Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka's resignation.

Vietnam postponed international issuance because officials considered borrowing costs too high. Finance Minister Ngo Van Tuan said preparations and investor engagement would continue for better conditions; discussions had concerned a possible sovereign dollar sale of as much as $1 billion. Serbia took a more immediate policy step, unexpectedly raising its benchmark a quarter-point to 6% against unanimous forecasts for no change. It cited energy pass-through and currency pressure as October inflation accelerated to 4.4% from 4.1%. Turkey instead raised its end-2027 inflation forecast and target to 21% from 15%, while Governor Fatih Karahan said the revision did not change policy following October's rate cut to 36%.

## Recovery Values and Perpetual Capital Face New Tests

Citgo's new earnings and cash outlook intensified speculation that Elliott-backed Amber Energy's planned $5.9 billion acquisition would be revisited. The refiner expects as much as $7 billion of cash at year-end and full-year EBITDA of up to $7.5 billion, against its previous $5.8 billion forecast. The oil-price windfall has substantially increased the value underlying a sale intended to settle $8.8 billion of creditor claims.

Some Citgo-linked debt traded as high as 120 cents on the dollar, about 6% above its value under the takeover agreement. The bonds due in 2020 are secured by 50.1% of the parent company. Barclays' estimates had put payments at $128 per unit of principal for holders signing the agreement and $108 for others if the transaction closed in June; payments have increased 0.75% for each month of delay. A narrowing market-price gap between the groups reflected expectations of reconsideration.

The legal and recovery questions remain separate. An appeals court upheld the bonds' validity in October, while Venezuela and others continue appealing the selection of Amber's bid. Caledonia trader Francesco Marani said holders could seek an original claim estimated at 170-180 cents if the sale failed, while stressing that settlement need not equal that amount. The higher operating value strengthens creditors' negotiating expectations without fixing the final distribution.

A newly public KPMG audit clarified another part of Venezuela's financial position. More than $12.1 billion of petroleum and gas proceeds passed through a Treasury-administered account during the first nine months of 2026; nearly 99% of deposited funds, or $12.11 billion, had been disbursed. Most payments went through Venezuelan foreign-exchange auctions, with about $133 million paid directly to government vendors. The audit described the funds as Venezuela's sovereign property, with permitted use subject to authority exercised by Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

SAS faces a different dispute over the survival of creditor claims. Holders representing more than half of a 127.2 million Swiss franc subordinated perpetual bond argue that the airline's U.S. Chapter 11 restructuring was not recognized in Switzerland. Their November 5 letter seeks enforcement after unpaid annual interest since January 2023. They also argue the issuing SAS Consortium was excluded from the parallel Swedish restructuring. SAS confirmed receipt and said it was reviewing the letter; its restructuring had treated the bonds as extinguished with no recovery. The dispute could complicate Air France-KLM's planned increase to a 60.5% controlling stake.

New research on $22 billion of fixed-for-life U.S. bank preferred shares highlighted a different form of extension exposure. The group has lost 8.5% in total-return terms this year and trades around 61 cents on the dollar on average. Issuers have skipped available calls as replacing sub-5% coupons would cost more. Morgan Stanley's $1.3 billion issue, callable in January, was indicated at 61.4 cents; U.S. Bancorp's 3.75% series stood around 55 cents. The contractual permanence of coupons makes the economics of calling central to recovery prospects, while newly issued fixed-for-life preferreds have carried average coupons of 6.69% this year.

Germany's Bundesbank separately warned that commercial-property prices could fall again if rates rose or redemptions forced funds to sell. It said the recovery since 2024 had involved relatively few transactions concentrated in better-quality buildings, with office and retail prices recently edging lower. Property funds accounted for 13% of German mutual-fund assets in August, against 21% at end-2023. Withdrawal restrictions at several funds pointed to tighter liquidity, while lender Deutsche Pfandbriefbank expected no near-term improvement in conditions.

## Forward Market Significance

Friday's U.S. producer-price release will provide the next observation of upstream inflation after the Treasury selloff and oil rebound. The distinction between energy costs, technology-related inputs and broader pricing pressure remains important to the December debate. Hammack has argued for more frequent conventional increases while leaving stronger action conditional on falling behind; Daly's business contacts suggest broader pass-through is under consideration. The next price evidence will arrive with futures already pricing quarter-point increases in December, January and March.

Japan's Monday GDP release will test the demand side of Asada's caution before the December 17-18 BOJ meeting. Economists expect consumer spending to decline for the first time in nearly two years. The combination of that observation, October's producer-price acceleration and a yen near 160 will shape the balance between imported cost pressure and domestic spending. Renewed intervention remains an independent currency risk, with authorities focused on the character of moves rather than announcing a fixed exchange-rate trigger.

Nvidia's November 17 earnings will be its first major financial test under interim leadership, alongside questions about future supplier support and the delayed financing platform. Anthropic's offering and CoreWeave's proposed secured syndication will separately test whether institutional demand becomes executable funding on acceptable terms. Nvidia's pledged purchase of about $10 billion of Anthropic shares remains a specific commitment under scrutiny following Huang's departure.

Fiscal decisions have their own deadlines. Brazil plans a constitutional amendment before year-end, while Colombia needs its rescue legislation approved this year for measures to operate in early 2027. Ghana's planned December 31 payments will test the implementation of its early-repayment pledge. The European Commission intends to present Ukraine's 2027 financing proposal and a new Russia-sanctions package before the November 26-27 European Council meeting; the funding instrument and burden-sharing remain under discussion.

Oil diplomacy and shipping security remain capable of changing the inflation outlook independently of scheduled data. The large U.S. inventory increases have improved the immediate domestic stock position, while Trump's tougher stance has reduced confidence in a negotiated resolution. The durability of restored regional supply and the terms of any diplomatic progress remain unresolved as markets enter the next Asian session.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries sell off as oil and Fed tightening calls overturn the early haven bid
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries reversed an early haven bid tied to Nvidia's leadership crisis as oil rebounded and Fed officials reinforced the case for further tightening. The 2-year yield rose 14.37 basis points to 4.8814%, and the 10-year increased 13.75 basis points to 5.1271%. The 2- to 10-year spread narrowed 0.62 basis point to 24.57 basis points. Higher real borrowing costs accounted for most of the 10-year move: the TIPS yield rose 9.59 basis points, while inflation compensation increased 4.16 basis points.

Trump's assertion that the U.S. could forgo an Iran agreement weakened diplomatic optimism and lifted oil, even with large U.S. inventory increases. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack favored more frequent, smaller rate increases; San Francisco's Mary Daly expected further tightening would probably be necessary as businesses considered passing on costs. Low layoffs and sharply weaker home sales showed uneven effects of existing restraint, leaving December's increase size contested.

Nvidia removed Jensen Huang and named Colette Kress interim CEO. Its default-protection costs fell after an initial rise as traders considered whether the transition would curb borrowing and support for other AI companies. Its announced $500 billion financing platform had produced no deals, with partners seeking residual-value support beyond the proposed 25% ceiling. Alphabet nevertheless completed almost $4 billion-equivalent of Asian local-currency borrowing, and CoreWeave's bonds improved as more detailed secured-financing terms emerged. Investor capacity and the execution of supplier-backed funding remain central uncertainties.
